commands.dependencies: cd hosted && HEX_OFFLINE=1 MIX_ENV=test mix deps.get
commands.postgres: initdb --no-locale -E UTF8 -A trust in owned scratch. Foreground PostgreSQL on ephemeral IPv4 loopback with UTC session timezone, jit off, 32 MB shared buffers and synthetic browser/catalog and ledger fixture roles. Set MIXER_BROWSER_STORAGE_PORT, MIXER_RELEASE_LEDGER_TEST_PORT and MIXER_BROWSER_CATALOG_FIXTURE_ROOT for the test subprocess.
commands.goReference: cd services && GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOPROXY=off go test -count=1 ./protocol ./release
commands.goWire: cd services && GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOPROXY=off go run <owned-scratch>/verify-wire.go protocol/testdata/signed-release-v3.json <owned-scratch>/wire.json

observations: Disabled startup returned 404 on both routes and started no delivery Repo. Enabled startup used the regular Phoenix application and listener.

A fixture PKCE browser session staged two signed envelopes through CustomerArtifacts and committed assignments 7 and 8 through RuntimeOwner.publish_release. Neither staged artifact was readable before publication. A still-staged artifact remained 404 after a different commit.

HTTP GET for the eligible installation returned the exact signed assignment and a relative exact-tenant URL. The artifact URL returned the exact immutable signed envelope and payload. After sequence 8 superseded sequence 7, both committed artifacts remained readable.

Excluded installation, wrong runtime, wrong channel, wrong tenant and revoked current trust yielded empty 204 offers. Both foreign tenant axes denied artifact delivery. Extra, duplicate and percent-encoded duplicate query keys returned 400. Revoking the artifact root denied both reads; revoking the assignment root denied offers while the valid previously committed artifact stayed readable.

The reader lacked direct artifact SELECT, head UPDATE and publication DELETE privileges. The ordinary browser writer lacked EXECUTE on the public artifact function. A direct foreign-tenant function invocation returned no rows. The function preserved all four caller GUC values within one still-open transaction.
After stopping and starting Phoenix on the same PostgreSQL database, sequence 8 and both previously committed artifacts were served again, and cohort exclusion persisted.

wireOracle.checked: The existing Go decoder and v3 manifest/assignment verifiers consumed the actual Phoenix responses, checked the relative exact-tenant URL and validated the same cohort buckets using protocol.Cohort.

earlierAttempts.result: The isolated collector omitted the existing browser catalog definer role. The fixture also needed separate evidence subdirectories when both browser tests ran in one command.

PostgreSQL refused a function-level SET clause for an unregistered authorization parameter under the non-login migration owner. The successor uses statement-local settings and restores the caller values before returning.

The first request after Phoenix restart reached the endpoint before the delivery connection was ready and returned 503. The final restart check waited for the independent Repo connection before checking readback.

remaining: Parent owns independent review and source selection. This is a local read slice of L05, using test-only signing and one loopback target. The restart kept PostgreSQL running. L05 acceptance and production qualification remain pending.
